title.zh: 卷一 本紀第一: 太祖上
title.raw: 卷一 本紀第一: 太祖上 Volume 1 Annals 1: Taizu 1

sentences.zh: 太祖耶律阿保機上

translations.literal: Taizu Yelü Abaoji, Part One
translations.idiomatic: Annals of Taizu Yelü Abaoji, Part One

sentences.zh: 太祖大聖大明神烈天皇帝，姓耶律氏，諱億，字阿保機，小字啜裏只，契丹迭剌部霞瀨益石烈鄉耶律弭里人。

translations.literal: The Taizu, Great Sage, Great Brightness, Divine Martial, Heavenly Emperor — surname Yelü, taboo name Yi, courtesy name Abaoji, childhood name Chuilizhi — was a native of Yelü Mili village, Xiasiyishi Lie, Dieci Department of the Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu, styled the Great Sage and Bright Divine Martial Heavenly Emperor, bore the surname Yelü; his given name was Yi, his courtesy name Abaoji, and his childhood name Chuilizhi. He came from Yelü Mili in the Xiasiyishi Lie of the Khitan Dieci branch.

sentences.zh: <一>德祖皇帝長子，母曰宣簡皇后蕭氏。

translations.literal: <1> He was the eldest son of Emperor Dezu; his mother was Empress Xuanjian, née Xiao.
translations.idiomatic: <1> He was the eldest son of Emperor Dezu, born to Empress Xuanjian of the Xiao clan.

sentences.zh: 唐咸通十三年生。

translations.literal: He was born in the thirteenth year of the Tang Xiantong reign.
translations.idiomatic: He was born in the thirteenth year of Emperor Yizong's Xiantong era (872).

sentences.zh: 初，母夢日墮懷中，有娠。

translations.literal: At the beginning, his mother dreamed that the sun fell into her bosom, and she conceived.
translations.idiomatic: Before his birth, his mother dreamed that the sun dropped into her breast, and afterward she became pregnant.

sentences.zh: 及生，室有神光異香，體如三歲兒，即能匍匐。

translations.literal: When he was born, the room had divine light and strange fragrance; his body was like that of a three-year-old child, and he could crawl at once.
translations.idiomatic: At his birth, divine light filled the room and a strange fragrance hung in the air. His body was already like a three-year-old's, and he could crawl immediately.

sentences.zh: 祖母簡獻皇后異之，鞠為己子。

translations.literal: His grandmother, Empress Jianxian, regarded him as extraordinary and reared him as her own son.
translations.idiomatic: His grandmother Empress Jianxian took him for a prodigy and raised him as if he were her own child.

sentences.zh: 常匿於別幕，塗其面，不令他人見。

translations.literal: She often hid him in a separate tent, smeared his face, and did not allow others to see him.
translations.idiomatic: She kept him hidden in a separate tent, darkened his face with ash, and forbade anyone else to look upon him.

sentences.zh: 三月能行；

translations.literal: At three months he could walk;
translations.idiomatic: By three months he could walk;

sentences.zh: 而能言，知未然事。

translations.literal: and he could speak, and knew things before they happened.
translations.idiomatic: and soon he could speak and foretell events yet to come.

sentences.zh: 自謂左右若有神人翼衛。

translations.literal: He claimed that on his left and right there seemed to be divine beings guarding him with wings.
translations.idiomatic: He said that divine guardians seemed to hover at his sides, winged and vigilant.

sentences.zh: 雖齠齔，言必及世務。

translations.literal: Although he was still in childhood, his words always touched upon affairs of state.
translations.idiomatic: Even as a child with baby teeth, he spoke always of public affairs.

sentences.zh: 時伯父當國，疑輒咨焉。

translations.literal: At that time his uncle held power over the state; whenever in doubt he would consult him.
translations.idiomatic: His uncle then governed the Khitan, and whenever uncertain he sought the boy's counsel.

sentences.zh: 既長，身長九尺，豐上銳下，目光射人，關弓三百斤。

translations.literal: When he had grown up, he stood nine chi tall, broad above and tapering below; his gaze pierced people, and he could draw a bow of three hundred jin.
translations.idiomatic: Grown to manhood, he stood nine chi in height — broad-shouldered above, lean below — with a gaze that struck men like an arrow and strength enough to draw a three-hundred-jin bow.

sentences.zh: 為撻馬沙裏。

translations.literal: He served as tamun shar.
translations.idiomatic: He held the office of tamun shar.

sentences.zh: 時小黃室韋不附，太祖以計降之。

translations.literal: At that time the Lesser Yellow Shiwei did not submit; Taizu subdued them by stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: When the Lesser Yellow Shiwei refused submission, Taizu took them by strategy.

sentences.zh: 伐越兀及烏古、六奚、比沙諸部，克之。

translations.literal: He attacked the Yuewu, Wugu, Liuxi, Bisha, and other tribes, and conquered them.
translations.idiomatic: He marched against Yuewu and the Wugu, Liuxi, and Bisha tribes, among others, and brought them to heel.

sentences.zh: 國人號阿主沙裏。

translations.literal: The people of the state called him Azhu Shar.
translations.idiomatic: His countrymen gave him the name Azhu Shar.

sentences.zh: 唐天復元年，歲辛酉，痕德可汗立，以太祖為本部夷離，專征討，連破室韋、于厥及奚帥轄剌哥，俘獲甚眾。

translations.literal: In the first year of the Tang Tianfu reign, the year xinyou, Hende Khan was enthroned and appointed Taizu yilijin of the native tribe, put in charge of campaigns; he repeatedly defeated the Shiwei, Yujue, and the Xi chieftain Xialage, capturing many prisoners.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Tang Tianfu era (901), the xinyou year, Hende Khan came to power and made Taizu yilijin of his own branch, entrusting him with military command. Taizu in succession broke the Shiwei and Yujue and the Xi leader Xialage, taking vast numbers captive.

sentences.zh: 冬十月，授大迭烈府夷離。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter, he was appointed yilijin of the Great Dieci Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, in the tenth month, he was given the post of yilijin of the Great Dieci Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 明年秋七月，以兵四十萬伐河東代北，<二>攻下九郡，獲生口九萬五千，駝、馬、牛、羊不可勝紀。

translations.literal: The following year, in the seventh month of autumn, with four hundred thousand troops he attacked Hedong and the north of Dai; <2> he captured nine commanderies, taking ninety-five thousand captives, and camels, horses, cattle, and sheep beyond numbering.
translations.idiomatic: The next autumn, in the seventh month, he led four hundred thousand men against Hedong and northern Dai, <2> seized nine commanderies, took ninety-five thousand captives, and won camels, horses, cattle, and sheep past all count.

sentences.zh: 九月，城龍化州於潢河之南，始建開教寺。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, he walled Longhua Prefecture south of the Huang River and for the first time built Kaijiao Temple.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he fortified Longhua Prefecture on the south bank of the Huang River and founded Kaijiao Temple.

sentences.zh: 明年春，伐女直，下之，獲其戶三百。

translations.literal: The following spring, he attacked the Jurchen, subjugated them, and captured three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: The next spring he campaigned against the Jurchen, brought them down, and took three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 九月，復攻下河東懷遠等軍。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, he again attacked and captured the Huaiyuan Army and other Hedong garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he renewed the assault on Hedong and took the Huaiyuan garrison and others.

sentences.zh: 冬十月，引軍略至薊北，俘獲以還。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter, he led his army in a raid as far as north of Ji and returned with captives and booty.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, in the tenth month, he pushed his forces in a foray to the north of Ji and returned laden with prisoners and plunder.

sentences.zh: 先是德祖俘奚七千戶，徙饒樂之清河，至是創為奚迭剌部，分十三縣。

translations.literal: Previously Dezu had captured seven thousand Xi households and moved them to Qinghe in Raole; at this time they were established as the Xi Dieci branch and divided into thirteen districts.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Dezu had taken seven thousand Xi households and resettled them at Qinghe in Raole; now they were organized into the Xi Dieci branch, divided into thirteen counties.

sentences.zh: 遂拜太祖于越、總知軍國事。

translations.literal: Taizu was then appointed yue and given overall charge of military and state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu was thereupon made yue, with full authority over army and state.

sentences.zh: 明年歲甲子，三月，廣龍化州之東城。

translations.literal: The following year, the jiazi year, in the third month, the eastern wall of Longhua Prefecture was expanded.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, a jiazi year, in the third month the eastern quarter of Longhua Prefecture was enlarged.

sentences.zh: 九月，討黑車子室韋，唐盧龍軍節度使劉仁恭發兵數萬，遣養子趙霸來拒。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, he campaigned against the Black-Cart Shiwei; Liu Rengong, Military Governor of the Tang Lulong Army, sent tens of thousands of troops and dispatched his adopted son Zhao Ba to resist.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he marched against the Black-Cart Shiwei. Liu Rengong, Tang governor of the Lulong Army, raised tens of thousands of men and sent his adopted son Zhao Ba to meet him.

sentences.zh: 霸至武州，太祖諜知之，伏勁兵桃山下。

translations.literal: When Ba reached Wuzhou, Taizu learned of it through spies and hid crack troops below Peach Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Ba reached Wuzhou; Taizu, warned by his scouts, lay in wait with elite troops beneath Peach Mountain.

sentences.zh: 遣室韋人牟裏詐稱其酋長所遣，約霸兵會平原。

translations.literal: He sent a Shiwei man named Moli, who falsely claimed to have been sent by his chieftain, to arrange a meeting with Ba's forces on the plain.
translations.idiomatic: He sent a Shiwei named Moli to pose as an envoy from the chieftain and invite Ba's army to a rendezvous on the open plain.

sentences.zh: 既至，四面伏發，擒霸，殲其眾，乘勝大破室韋。

translations.literal: When they arrived, the hidden troops sprang up on all sides; they captured Ba, annihilated his force, and pressing the victory routed the Shiwei.
translations.idiomatic: When Ba came, ambushers rose on every side. They took Ba prisoner, wiped out his army, and drove on to shatter the Shiwei.

sentences.zh: 明年七月，復討黑車子室韋。

translations.literal: The following year, in the seventh month, he again campaigned against the Black-Cart Shiwei.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, in the seventh month, he returned to punish the Black-Cart Shiwei.

sentences.zh: 唐河東節度使李克用遣通事康令德乞盟。

translations.literal: Li Keyong, Military Governor of Hedong under the Tang, sent the interpreter Kang Lingde to request an alliance.
translations.idiomatic: Li Keyong, Tang's Hedong governor, sent his interpreter Kang Lingde to sue for an alliance.

sentences.zh: 冬十月，太祖以騎兵七萬會克用於雲州，宴酣，克用借兵以報劉仁恭木瓜澗之役，太祖許之。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter, Taizu with seventy thousand cavalry met Keyong at Yunzhou; when the banquet was well underway, Keyong asked to borrow troops to avenge his defeat by Liu Rengong at Mugua Ravine, and Taizu agreed.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, in the tenth month, Taizu brought seventy thousand horsemen to meet Keyong at Yunzhou. Over wine Keyong asked for troops to settle the score with Liu Rengong at Mugua Ravine, and Taizu consented.

sentences.zh: 易袍馬，約為兄弟。

translations.literal: They exchanged robes and horses and pledged brotherhood.
translations.idiomatic: They exchanged cloaks and mounts and swore themselves brothers.

sentences.zh: 及進兵擊仁恭，撥數州，盡徙其民以歸。

translations.literal: When they advanced to attack Rengong, they seized several prefectures and moved all the people away with them.
translations.idiomatic: Marching on Rengong, they overran several prefectures and carried off the entire populace.

sentences.zh: 明年二月，復擊劉仁恭。

translations.literal: The following year, in the second month, they again attacked Liu Rengong.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, in the second month, they struck Liu Rengong once more.

sentences.zh: 還，襲山北奚，破之。

translations.literal: On the return, they raided the Xi north of the mountains and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: On the homeward march they fell upon the mountain-north Xi and broke them.

sentences.zh: 汴州朱全忠遣人浮海奉書幣、衣帶、珍玩來聘。

translations.literal: Zhu Quanzhong of Bianzhou sent men by sea bearing letters, gifts, robes and belts, and precious objects to offer friendship.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Quanzhong of Bianzhou dispatched envoys by sea with letters, tribute gifts, robes, sashes, and curiosities to propose alliance.

sentences.zh: 十一月，遣偏師討奚、諸部及東北女直之未附者，悉破降之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, he sent a detached force to campaign against the Xi and various tribes, and the unsubmitted Jurchen of the northeast; all were defeated and made to submit.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month he sent a subsidiary army against the Xi and allied tribes, and against Jurchen in the northeast still outside his sway; all were crushed and brought to surrender.

sentences.zh: 十二月，痕德可汗殂，群臣奉遺命請立太祖。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Hende Khan died; the ministers, obeying his final command, asked that Taizu be enthroned.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Hende Khan died. The ministers, following his dying wish, pressed Taizu to take the throne.

sentences.zh: 曷魯等勸進。

translations.literal: Helu and others urged him to accept.
translations.idiomatic: Helu and others pressed him to ascend.

sentences.zh: 太祖三讓，從之。

translations.literal: Taizu declined three times, then acquiesced.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu refused thrice before yielding to them.

sentences.zh: 元年春正月庚寅，命有司設壇于如迂王集會堝，<三>燔柴告天，即皇帝位。

translations.literal: In the first year, on gengyin day in the first month of spring, he ordered officials to set up an altar at the Ru'erwang Assembly Mound; <3> he burned sacrificial wood to announce Heaven and took the imperial throne.
translations.idiomatic: In his first year, on the gengyin day of the first spring month, he had officials erect an altar at the Ru'erwang Assembly Mound, <3> offered burnt sacrifices to Heaven, and ascended the throne.

sentences.zh: 尊母蕭氏為皇太后，立皇后蕭氏。

translations.literal: He honored his mother, née Xiao, as Empress Dowager and installed Empress Xiao.
translations.idiomatic: He raised his mother of the Xiao clan to Empress Dowager and crowned an Empress Xiao.

sentences.zh: 北宰相蕭轄剌、南宰相耶律歐裏思率群臣上尊號曰天皇帝，後曰地皇后。

translations.literal: The Northern Chancellor Xiao Xialage and the Southern Chancellor Yelü Oulisi led the ministers in offering the honorific titles Heavenly Emperor and Earth Empress.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Chancellor Xiao Xialage and Southern Chancellor Yelü Oulisi, at the head of the court, presented the elevated titles Heavenly Emperor for him and Earth Empress for her.

sentences.zh: 庚子，詔皇族承遙輦氏九帳為第十帳。

translations.literal: On gengzi day, an edict proclaimed that the imperial clan would succeed the nine tents of the Yaolian clan as the tenth tent.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi day he decreed that the royal house should take its place as a tenth tent, succeeding the nine tents of the Yaolian line.

sentences.zh: 二月戊午，以從弟迭栗底為迭烈府夷離。

translations.literal: On wuwu day in the second month, he appointed his younger cousin Dielidi yilijin of the Dieci Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu day of the second month he named his cousin Dielidi yilijin of the Dieci Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 是月，征黑車子室韋，降其八部。

translations.literal: That month, he campaigned against the Black-Cart Shiwei and brought their eight tribes to submission.
translations.idiomatic: That same month he marched on the Black-Cart Shiwei and received the submission of all eight of their tribes.

sentences.zh: 夏四月丁未朔，唐梁王朱全忠廢其主，尋弑之，<四>自立為帝，國號梁，遣使來告。

translations.literal: On dingwei, the first day of the fourth month of summer, Zhu Quanzhong, Prince of Liang under the Tang, deposed his sovereign and soon killed him; <4> he declared himself emperor, taking the dynastic name Liang, and sent envoys to announce it.
translations.idiomatic: On the dingwei new moon of the fourth summer month, Zhu Quanzhong, Tang's Prince of Liang, deposed his lord and shortly afterward murdered him; <4> he proclaimed himself emperor under the name Liang and sent envoys with the news.

sentences.zh: 劉仁恭子守光囚其父，自稱幽州盧龍軍節度使。

translations.literal: Liu Rengong's son Shouguang imprisoned his father and styled himself Military Governor of Youzhou and the Lulong Army.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shouguang, son of Liu Rengong, locked up his father and declared himself governor of Youzhou and the Lulong Army.

sentences.zh: 秋七月乙酉，其兄平州刺史守奇率其眾數千人來降，命置之平盧城。

translations.literal: On yiyou day in the seventh month of autumn, his elder brother Shouqi, Governor of Pingzhou, led several thousand of his followers to surrender, and they were ordered settled at Pinglu City.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou day in the seventh autumn month his elder brother Shouqi, prefect of Pingzhou, came over with several thousand men and was resettled at Pinglu City.

sentences.zh: 冬十月乙巳，討黑車子室韋，破之。

translations.literal: On yisi day in the tenth month of winter, he campaigned against the Black-Cart Shiwei and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi day that winter, in the tenth month, he attacked the Black-Cart Shiwei and broke them.

sentences.zh: 二年春正月癸酉朔，禦正殿受百官及諸國使朝。

translations.literal: On guiyou, the first day of the first month of spring in the second year, he received homage in the main hall from officials and envoys of various states.
translations.idiomatic: On the guiyou new moon of the second year's first spring month, he held court in the main hall to receive the obeisance of officials and foreign envoys.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，始置惕隱，典族屬，以皇弟撒剌為之。

translations.literal: On xinsi day, the office of tiyin was first established to oversee clan affairs, and his imperial brother Salaci was appointed to it.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi day he created the office of tiyin to govern the clans and appointed his brother Salaci to the post.

sentences.zh: 河東李克用卒，<五>子存襲，遣使吊慰。

translations.literal: Li Keyong of Hedong died; <5> his son Cunxu succeeded him, and envoys were sent to offer condolences.
translations.idiomatic: Li Keyong of Hedong died; <5> his son Li Cunxu took his place, and Taizu sent envoys with condolences.

sentences.zh: 夏五月癸酉，詔撒剌討烏丸、黑車子室韋。

translations.literal: On guiyou day in the fifth month of summer, an edict ordered Salaci to campaign against the Wuhuan and Black-Cart Shiwei.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou day of the fifth summer month he commanded Salaci against the Wuhuan and the Black-Cart Shiwei.

sentences.zh: 秋八月壬子，幽州進合歡瓜。

translations.literal: On renzi day in the eighth month of autumn, Youzhou presented a hehuan melon.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi day in the eighth autumn month, Youzhou sent tribute of a twin-fused melon.

sentences.zh: 冬十月己亥朔，建明王樓。

translations.literal: On jihai, the first day of the tenth month of winter, the Bright King Tower was built.
translations.idiomatic: On the jihai new moon of the tenth winter month, he erected the Bright King Tower.

sentences.zh: 築長城於鎮東海口。

translations.literal: A long wall was built at the eastern sea mouth of Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: He constructed a long wall at Zhendong's seaward mouth.

sentences.zh: 遣輕兵取吐渾叛入室韋者。

translations.literal: Light troops were dispatched to capture Tuyuhun rebels who had fled into Shiwei territory.
translations.idiomatic: He sent light cavalry to seize Tuyuhun rebels who had crossed into Shiwei lands.

sentences.zh: 三年春正月，幸遼東。

translations.literal: In the first month of spring in the third year, he visited Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year's first spring month he toured Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 二月丁酉朔，梁遣郎公遠來聘。

translations.literal: On dingyou, the first day of the second month, Liang sent Lang Gongyuan on a diplomatic mission.
translations.idiomatic: On the dingyou new moon of the second month, Liang dispatched Lang Gongyuan as envoy.

sentences.zh: 三月，滄州節度使劉守文為弟守光所攻，遣人來乞兵討之。

translations.literal: In the third month, Liu Shouwen, Military Governor of Cangzhou, was attacked by his brother Shouguang and sent men to request troops to campaign against him.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Liu Shouwen, governor of Cangzhou, came under attack from his brother Shouguang and sent asking for troops to strike back.

sentences.zh: 命皇弟舍利素、夷離蕭敵魯以兵會守文於北淖口。

translations.literal: He ordered his imperial brother Sheli Su and the yilijin Xiao Dilu to lead troops to join Shouwen at Beinao Mouth.
translations.idiomatic: He commanded his brother Sheli Su and the yilijin Xiao Dilu to march and rendezvous with Shouwen at Beinao Mouth.

sentences.zh: 進至橫海軍近澱，一鼓破之，守光潰去。

translations.literal: Advancing to the marshland near the Henghai Army, they broke the enemy at the first assault and Shouguang fled in rout.
translations.idiomatic: Pushing to the flats near the Henghai garrison, they shattered the foe at a single drumbeat and Shouguang broke and ran.

sentences.zh: 因名北淖口為會盟口。

translations.literal: Because of this, Beinao Mouth was renamed Alliance Mouth.
translations.idiomatic: Beinao Mouth was therefore renamed Alliance Mouth.

sentences.zh: 夏四月乙卯，詔左僕射韓知古建碑龍化州大廣寺以紀功德。

translations.literal: On yimao day in the fourth month of summer, an edict ordered Left Vice Director Han Zhigu to erect a stele at the Daguan Temple of Longhua Prefecture to record meritorious deeds.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao day of the fourth summer month he ordered Vice Premier Han Zhigu to raise a stele at Longhua Prefecture's Daguan Temple commemorating his achievements.

sentences.zh: 五月甲申，置羊城於炭山之北以通市易。

translations.literal: On jiashen day in the fifth month, a sheep market was established north of Coal Mountain to facilitate trade.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen day in the fifth month he founded a sheep market north of Coal Mountain for commerce.

sentences.zh: 冬十月己巳，遣鷹軍討黑車子室韋，破之。

translations.literal: On jisi day in the tenth month of winter, the Hawk Army was sent to campaign against the Black-Cart Shiwei and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi day that winter, in the tenth month, he sent the Hawk Army against the Black-Cart Shiwei and broke them.

sentences.zh: 西北娘改部族進挽車人。

translations.literal: The Nianggai tribe of the northwest presented ox-cart drivers as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: The Nianggai tribe from the northwest offered cart-drivers in tribute.

sentences.zh: 四年秋七月戊子朔，以后兄蕭敵魯為北府宰相。

translations.literal: On wuzi, the first day of the seventh month of autumn in the fourth year, his empress's elder brother Xiao Dilu was appointed Northern Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuzi new moon of the fourth year's seventh autumn month he named the Empress's elder brother Xiao Dilu Northern Chancellor.

sentences.zh: 后族為相自此始。

translations.literal: From this time the empress's clan began to hold the chancellorship.
translations.idiomatic: Thus began the custom of appointing the Empress's kin as chancellor.

sentences.zh: 冬十月，烏馬山奚庫支及查剌底、鋤勃德等叛，討平之。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter, the Xi chieftains Kuge, Chaladi, and Chubode of Wumashan rebelled and were suppressed.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, in the tenth month, the Wumashan Xi leaders Kuge, Chaladi, and Chubode rose in rebellion and were put down.

sentences.zh: 五年春正月丙戌朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: On bingxu, the first day of the first month of spring in the fifth year, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingxu new moon of the fifth year's first spring month the sun was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 丙申，上親征西部奚。

translations.literal: On bingshen day, the Emperor personally campaigned against the western Xi.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen day the Emperor took the field in person against the western Xi.

sentences.zh: 奚阻險，叛服不常，數招諭弗聽。

translations.literal: The Xi held difficult terrain; their submission and rebellion were inconstant, and repeated summons and persuasion went unheeded.
translations.idiomatic: The Xi barricaded themselves in rugged country, wavering between rebellion and submission; repeated appeals brought no answer.

sentences.zh: 是役所向輒下，遂分兵討東部奚，亦平之。

translations.literal: In this campaign wherever he went he prevailed; he then divided his forces to campaign against the eastern Xi and pacified them as well.
translations.idiomatic: In that campaign he took every stronghold he met; he then split his army to subdue the eastern Xi and pacified them too.

sentences.zh: 於是盡有奚、之地。

translations.literal: Thus he came to possess all the lands of the Xi and Shiwei.
translations.idiomatic: He now held the full territory of the Xi and Shiwei.

sentences.zh: 東際海，南暨白檀，西松漠，北抵潢水，凡五部，咸入版籍。

translations.literal: It reached the sea on the east, touched Baitan on the south, Songmo on the west, and the Huang River on the north; all five divisions were entered on the registers.
translations.idiomatic: Eastward it ran to the sea, south to Baitan, west to Songmo, north to the Huang River — five divisions in all, every one entered on the tax rolls.

sentences.zh: 三月，次灤河，刻石紀功。

translations.literal: In the third month, he halted at the Luan River and carved stone to record his achievements.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month he encamped on the Luan River and cut stone inscriptions to commemorate his victories.

sentences.zh: 復略地薊州。

translations.literal: He again raided the territory of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He again carried out a raid into Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 夏四月壬申，遣人使梁。

translations.literal: On renshen day in the fourth month of summer, envoys were sent to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen day of the fourth summer month he dispatched envoys to Liang.

sentences.zh: 五月，皇弟剌葛、迭剌、寅底石、安端謀反。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, his imperial brothers Cige, Dieci, Yindishi, and Anduan plotted rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month his brothers Cige, Dieci, Yindishi, and Anduan conspired to rebel.

sentences.zh: 安端妻粘睦姑知之，以告，得實。

translations.literal: Anduan's wife Nianmugu learned of it, reported it, and the plot was verified.
translations.idiomatic: Anduan's wife Nianmugu discovered the plot, informed the court, and the charge was proved true.

sentences.zh: 上不忍加誅，乃與諸弟登山刑牲，告天地為誓而赦其罪。

translations.literal: The Emperor could not bear to execute them; he therefore climbed a mountain with his brothers, sacrificed animals, announced Heaven and Earth as witnesses to an oath, and pardoned their crime.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to bring himself to punish them, he climbed a mountain with his brothers, offered sacrifice, swore before Heaven and Earth, and granted them pardon.

sentences.zh: 出剌葛為迭剌部夷離，封粘睦姑為晉國夫人。

translations.literal: Cige was sent out as yilijin of the Dieci branch, and Nianmugu was enfeoffed as Lady of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: He posted Cige as yilijin of the Dieci branch and ennobled Nianmugu as Lady of Jin.

sentences.zh: 秋七月壬午朔，斜離底及諸蕃使來貢。

translations.literal: On renwu, the first day of the seventh month of autumn, Xielidi and envoys of various tribes came to offer tribute.
translations.idiomatic: On the renwu new moon of the seventh autumn month, Xielidi and tribal envoys arrived with tribute.

sentences.zh: 八月甲子，劉守光僭號幽州，稱燕。

translations.literal: On jiazi day in the eighth month, Liu Shouguang usurped title at Youzhou and styled himself Yan.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi day in the eighth month Liu Shouguang seized the imperial style at Youzhou and proclaimed the state of Yan.

sentences.zh: 冬十月戊午，置鐵冶。

translations.literal: On wuwu day in the tenth month of winter, an iron foundry was established.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu day that winter, in the tenth month, he established an iron foundry.

sentences.zh: 十一月壬午，遣人使梁。

translations.literal: On renwu day in the eleventh month, envoys were sent to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu day in the eleventh month he again sent envoys to Liang.

sentences.zh: 六年春正月，以化葛為惕隱。

translations.literal: In the first month of spring in the sixth year, Huage was appointed tiyin.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year's first spring month he made Huage tiyin.

sentences.zh: 二月戊午，親征劉守光。

translations.literal: On wuwu day in the second month, he personally campaigned against Liu Shouguang.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu day of the second month he took the field in person against Liu Shouguang.

sentences.zh: 三月，至自幽州。

translations.literal: In the third month, he returned from Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month he came back from Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 夏四月，梁郢王友弑父自立。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of summer, You, Prince of Ying of Liang, killed his father and declared himself ruler.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth summer month Zhu Yougui, Liang's Prince of Ying, murdered his father and seized the throne.

sentences.zh: 秋七月丙午，親征術不姑，降之，俘獲以數萬計。

translations.literal: On bingwu day in the seventh month of autumn, he personally campaigned against Shibugu, made them submit, and took captives and booty numbering in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu day in the seventh autumn month he marched in person against Shibugu, received their surrender, and took prisoners and spoil by the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 命弟剌葛分兵攻平州。

translations.literal: He ordered his brother Cige to divide forces and attack Pingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He commanded his brother Cige to split off troops and strike Pingzhou.

sentences.zh: 八月壬辰，上次恩德山。

translations.literal: On renchen day in the eighth month, the Emperor halted at Mount Ende.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen day in the eighth month he encamped on Mount Ende.

sentences.zh: 皇子李胡生。

translations.literal: The Prince Li Hu was born.
translations.idiomatic: The prince Li Hu was born.

sentences.zh: 冬十月戊寅，剌葛破平州，還，復與迭剌、寅底石、安端等反。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter, on day wuyin, Cige captured Pingzhou; on returning, he again rebelled with Dieci, Yindishi, Anduan, and others.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, in the tenth month, on wuyin day, Cige took Pingzhou; coming back, he rose again with Dieci, Yindishi, Anduan, and the rest.

sentences.zh: 甲申，遣人使梁致祭。

translations.literal: On day jiashen, envoys were dispatched to Liang to present sacrificial offerings.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen day he sent envoys to Liang with offerings for the rites.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，還次北阿魯山，聞諸弟以兵阻道，引軍南趨十七濼。

translations.literal: On day renchen, returning he halted at North Aru Mountain; hearing his younger brothers had blocked the road with troops, he led the army south toward the Seventeen Marshes.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen day, marching back, he encamped at North Aru Mountain. Learning that his brothers had barred the route with soldiers, he turned the army south toward the Seventeen Marshes.

sentences.zh: 是日燔柴。

translations.literal: That day he burned sacrificial wood.
translations.idiomatic: That day he performed the burnt-offering rite.

sentences.zh: 翼日，次七渡河，諸弟各遣人謝罪。

translations.literal: The next day, he halted at the Seven Crossings River; each of his younger brothers sent someone to apologize.
translations.idiomatic: The following day he stopped at the Seven Crossings River, and each brother dispatched a messenger to beg forgiveness.

sentences.zh: 上猶矜憐，許以自新。

translations.literal: The Emperor still showed compassion and granted them permission to reform themselves.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor still looked on them with pity and allowed them to start anew.

sentences.zh: 是歲，以兵討兩冶，以所獲僧崇文等五十人歸西樓，建天雄寺以居之，以示天助雄武。

translations.literal: That year, with troops he campaigned against Liangye; bringing back the fifty captives including the monk Chongwen to Xilou, he built Tianxiong Temple to house them, as a sign that Heaven aided martial prowess.
translations.idiomatic: That year he took the field against Liangye. The fifty prisoners he won, among them the monk Chongwen, he brought back to Xilou and settled in a new Tianxiong Temple, proclaiming Heaven's blessing on his arms.

sentences.zh: 七年春正月甲辰朔，以用兵免朝。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, on the jiachen new moon of the first spring month, court audience was dispensed with because of military operations.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, on the jiachen new moon of the first spring month, the regular levee was canceled for war.

sentences.zh: 晉王李存撥幽州，擒劉守光。

translations.literal: Prince of Jin Li Cunxu besieged Youzhou and captured Liu Shouguang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Cunxu, Prince of Jin, invested Youzhou and took Liu Shouguang prisoner.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，王師次赤水城，弟剌葛等乞降。

translations.literal: On day jiayin, the imperial army halted at Chishui City; his younger brother Cige and others begged to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin day the royal host encamped at Chishui City, and Cige and his brothers sued for surrender.

sentences.zh: 上素服，乘赭白馬，以將軍耶律樂姑、轄剌僅阿缽為禦，解兵器、肅侍衛以受之，因加慰諭。

translations.literal: The Emperor wore plain white dress, mounted a reddish-white horse, and with Generals Yelü Legu and Xiala Jinebo as escorts, laid aside weapons and cleared his guard to receive them, then offered words of comfort and instruction.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor put on undyed robes, rode a sorrel-white horse, and with Generals Yelü Legu and Xiala Jinebo at his side laid down arms and thinned his guard to receive them, then spoke to them in reassurance.

sentences.zh: 剌葛等引退，上復數遣使撫慰。

translations.literal: Cige and the others withdrew; the Emperor again repeatedly sent envoys to console them.
translations.idiomatic: Cige and the rest withdrew, and the Emperor sent envoy after envoy to soothe them.

sentences.zh: 二月甲戌朔，梁均王友貞討殺其兄友，嗣立。

translations.literal: On the jiaxu new moon of the second month, Liang's Prince of Jun Zhu Youzhen overthrew and killed his elder brother Zhu Yougui and succeeded to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiaxu new moon of the second month, Zhu Youzhen, Liang's Prince of Jun, struck down his elder brother Zhu Yougui and seized the throne.

sentences.zh: 三月癸丑，次蘆水，弟迭剌哥圖為奚王，與安端擁千餘騎而至，紿稱入覲。

translations.literal: In the third month, on day guichou, he halted at Lu River; his younger brother Dieci Getu, installed as King of Xi, arrived with Anduan leading more than a thousand horsemen, falsely claiming to come for an audience.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on guichou day, he stopped at Lu River. His brother Dieci Getu, now styled King of Xi, came up with Anduan at the head of more than a thousand riders, pretending he meant to attend court.

sentences.zh: 上怒曰：「爾曹始謀逆亂，朕特恕之，使改過自新，尚爾反覆，將不利於朕！

translations.literal: The Emperor angrily said: "You at first plotted rebellion and disorder; I especially forgave you, that you might amend your faults and renew yourselves—yet you still waver and turn back; you mean harm to me!
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor flared in anger: "You first conspired in treason; I alone spared you so you might repent and reform—and still you turn and turn again, plotting against my person!

sentences.zh: 」遂拘之。

translations.literal: " He thereupon had them seized.
translations.idiomatic: " At once he had them seized.

sentences.zh: 以所部分隸諸軍。

translations.literal: Their followers were assigned to the various armies.
translations.idiomatic: Their men were distributed among the regiments.

sentences.zh: 而剌葛引其眾至乙室堇澱，具天子旗鼓，將自立，皇太后陰遣人諭令避去。

translations.literal: Meanwhile Cige led his followers to Yisijin Marsh, displayed the imperial banners and drums, and was about to declare himself emperor; the Empress Dowager secretly sent someone instructing them to withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Cige marched his force to Yisijin Marsh, raised the imperial banners and drums, and prepared to proclaim himself ruler; the Empress Dowager secretly sent word telling them to fall back.

sentences.zh: 會弭姑乃、懷裏陽言車駕且至，其眾驚潰，掠居民北走，上以兵追之。

translations.literal: When Migunai and Huailiyang reported that the imperial carriage was about to arrive, his force panicked and scattered, plundered the populace and fled north; the Emperor pursued with troops.
translations.idiomatic: Migunai and Huailiyang cried that the imperial train was near; the rebels broke in panic, looted the people, and fled north, and the Emperor gave chase with his army.

sentences.zh: 剌葛遣其党寅底石引兵徑趨行宮，焚其輜重、廬帳，縱兵大殺。

translations.literal: Cige sent his partisan Yindishi to lead troops straight to the traveling palace, burned its baggage and tents, and let his soldiers slaughter freely.
translations.idiomatic: Cige sent his follower Yindishi straight at the traveling palace with troops, burned wagons and tents, and turned his men loose to kill at will.

sentences.zh: 皇后急遣蜀古魯救之，<六>僅得天子旗鼓而已。

translations.literal: The empress urgently dispatched Shugulu to rescue it; <6> they recovered only the imperial banners and drums.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress hurried Shugulu to the rescue; <6> he salvaged nothing but the imperial banners and drums.

sentences.zh: 其党神速姑復劫西樓，焚明王樓。

translations.literal: His partisan Senshengu again raided Xilou and burned the Bright King Tower.
translations.idiomatic: Another rebel, Senshengu, struck Xilou again and put the Bright King Tower to the torch.

sentences.zh: 上至土河，秣馬休兵，若不為意。

translations.literal: The Emperor reached Tu River, fed the horses and rested the troops, as though unconcerned.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor came to Tu River, watered the horses and rested the men, showing no sign of alarm.

sentences.zh: 諸將請急追之，上曰：「俟其遠遁，人各懷土。

translations.literal: The generals urged immediate pursuit; the Emperor said: "Wait until they have fled far away; each man will yearn for home.
translations.idiomatic: His generals pressed for a hot pursuit, but the Emperor said: "Let them run far first; every man will begin to long for home.

sentences.zh: 懷土既切，其心必離，我軍乘之，破之必矣！

translations.literal: When homesickness grows acute, their hearts will surely split apart; our army will seize the moment—defeat is certain!
translations.idiomatic: When that longing bites deep, their hearts will break apart; then our troops will strike, and victory is assured!

sentences.zh: 」盡以先所獲資畜分賜將士，留夷離畢直裏姑總政務。

translations.literal: " He distributed all the livestock and goods taken earlier among officers and soldiers, and left Yilie Bilizhili in charge of government affairs.
translations.idiomatic: " He gave out all the herds and goods seized earlier to officers and rank and file alike, and left Yilie Bilizhili to govern affairs.

sentences.zh: 夏四月戊寅，北追剌葛。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of summer, on day wuyin, he pursued Cige northward.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth summer month, on wuyin day, he pressed north after Cige.

sentences.zh: 己卯，次弭裏，問諸弟面木葉山射鬼箭厭禳，<七>乃執叛人解裏向彼，亦以其法厭之。

translations.literal: On day jimao, he halted at Mili; inquiring about how his younger brothers, facing Mount Muye, shot ghost-arrows for exorcism, <7> he then seized the rebel Jieli and directed him there, likewise using that method to curse him.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao day he encamped at Mili. Learning how his brothers had faced Mount Muye and shot ghost-arrows to ward off evil, <7> he seized the rebel Jieli and sent him thither, treating him to the same rite of curse.

sentences.zh: 至達裏澱，選輕騎追及培只河，盡獲其黨輜重、生口。

translations.literal: Reaching Dali Marsh, he chose light cavalry and pursued to Peizhi River, capturing all their party's baggage and captives.
translations.idiomatic: At Dali Marsh he picked out light horsemen and ran the fugitives down to Peizhi River, taking all their baggage and prisoners.

sentences.zh: 先遣室韋及吐渾酋長撥剌、迪裏姑等五人分兵伏其前路，命北宰相迪裏古為先鋒進擊之。

translations.literal: He first sent five chiefs including the Shiwei and Tuguhun leaders Bola and Diligu to divide forces and ambush their forward route, ordering the Northern Chancellor Diligu as vanguard to advance and attack.
translations.idiomatic: First he posted five chieftains, among them the Shiwei and Tuguhun leaders Bola and Diligu, to split their men and lie in wait along the road ahead, while Northern Chancellor Diligu led the van in attack.

sentences.zh: 剌葛率兵逆戰，迪裏古以輕兵薄之。

translations.literal: Cige led troops to meet in battle; Diligu closed with light forces.
translations.idiomatic: Cige turned to fight; Diligu pressed him with a light detachment.

sentences.zh: 其弟遏古只臨陣，射數十人斃，眾莫敢前。

translations.literal: His younger brother Eguzhi on the battle line shot down dozens of men; none dared advance.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Eguzhi stood in the front rank and dropped dozens of men; no one dared press forward.

sentences.zh: 相拒至晡，眾乃潰。

translations.literal: They contested until late afternoon, then his force collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: The standoff lasted until dusk, then the rebel line gave way.

sentences.zh: 追至柴河，遂自焚其車乘廬帳而去。

translations.literal: Pursuit reached Chai River; they then burned their own carts, tents, and departed.
translations.idiomatic: The chase carried to Chai River; there the rebels burned their own wagons and tents and fled on.

sentences.zh: 前遇撥剌、迪裏姑等伏發，合擊，遂大敗之。

translations.literal: Ahead they met Bola, Diligu, and the other ambush as it sprang; combined attack then routed them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: Farther on they ran into Bola, Diligu, and the rest as the ambush closed; the converging blow shattered them completely.

sentences.zh: 剌葛奔潰，遺其所奪神帳於路，上見而拜奠之。

translations.literal: Cige fled in rout and abandoned on the road the divine tent he had seized; the Emperor saw it and bowed in offering.
translations.idiomatic: Cige broke and ran, leaving on the road the sacred tent he had stolen; the Emperor came upon it and bowed in reverent offering.

sentences.zh: 所獲生口盡縱歸本土。

translations.literal: All captives taken were released to return to their homelands.
translations.idiomatic: Every prisoner taken was freed to go home.

sentences.zh: 其党庫古只、磨朵皆面縛請罪。

translations.literal: His partisans Kuguzhi and Moduo were all bound facing forward and begged for pardon.
translations.idiomatic: His followers Kuguzhi and Moduo came forward with hands bound and pleaded for mercy.

sentences.zh: 師次劄堵河，大雨暴漲。

translations.literal: The army halted at Zhadu River; great rain swelled the waters suddenly.
translations.idiomatic: The host stopped at Zhadu River as a cloudburst sent the stream raging.

sentences.zh: 五月癸丑，遣北宰相迪輦率驍騎先渡。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on day guichou, he sent the Northern Chancellor Dilian leading crack horsemen to cross first.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on guichou day, he sent Northern Chancellor Dilian with elite cavalry to ford ahead.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，奏擒剌葛、涅裏袞阿缽於榆河，前北宰相蕭實魯、寅底石自剄不殊。

translations.literal: On day jiayin, it was reported that Cige and Nielihun A'bo were captured at Yu River; the former Northern Chancellor Xiao Shilu and Yindishi cut their own throats but did not die.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin day came word that Cige and Nielihun A'bo had been taken at Yu River; the former Northern Chancellor Xiao Shilu and Yindishi had slashed their own throats but survived.

sentences.zh: 遂以黑白羊祭天地。

translations.literal: Thereupon black and white sheep were used to sacrifice to Heaven and Earth.
translations.idiomatic: Black and white sheep were then offered to Heaven and Earth.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，剌葛、涅裏袞阿缽詣行在，以稿索自縛，牽羊望拜。

translations.literal: On day renxu, Cige and Nielihun A'bo came to the traveling court, bound themselves with straw ropes, led sheep and bowed from afar.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu day Cige and Nielihun A'bo appeared at the traveling court with straw cords about them, sheep in hand, bowing from a distance.

sentences.zh: 上還至大嶺。

translations.literal: The Emperor returned to Dal Ling.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor came back to Dal Ling.

sentences.zh: 時大軍久出，輜重不相屬，士卒煮馬駒、采野菜以為食，孳畜道斃者十七八，物價十倍，器服資貨委棄於楚裏河，狼藉數百里，因更剌葛名暴裏。

translations.literal: At that time the great army had been long abroad; baggage trains were not linked; soldiers boiled foals and gathered wild vegetables for food; livestock dying on the road were seven or eight in ten; prices rose tenfold; weapons, garments, goods and wealth were abandoned at Chuli River, scattered for hundreds of li; therefore Cige's name was changed to Baoli.
translations.idiomatic: The main army had been away too long; supply trains had fallen apart; men boiled colts and foraged wild greens to eat; seven or eight of every ten beasts died on the march; prices soared tenfold; arms, dress, goods, and treasure lay abandoned along Chuli River for hundreds of li in wreckage—and so Cige was renamed Baoli.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，至庫裏，以青牛白馬祭天地。

translations.literal: On day bingyin, reaching Kuli, he sacrificed with a blue ox and white horse to Heaven and Earth.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin day, arriving at Kuli, he offered a blue ox and a white horse to Heaven and Earth.

sentences.zh: 以生口六百、馬二千三百分賜大、小鶻軍。

translations.literal: Six hundred captives and two thousand three hundred horses were distributed as rewards to the Greater and Lesser Hawk Armies.
translations.idiomatic: Six hundred prisoners and twenty-three hundred horses were divided as booty between the Greater and Lesser Hawk Armies.

sentences.zh: 六月辛巳，至榆嶺，以轄賴縣人掃古非法殘民，磔之。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on day xinsi, reaching Yu Ling, because Saogu of Xialai County illegally tyrannized the people, he was dismembered.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on xinsi day, at Yu Ling, Saogu of Xialai County was torn apart for oppressing the people by unlawful means.

sentences.zh: 甲申，上登都庵山，撫其先奇首可汗遺跡，徘徊顧瞻而興歎焉。

translations.literal: On day jiashen, the Emperor ascended Du'an Mountain, touched the traces left by the former Qishi Khan, and wandered looking back, sighing with emotion.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen day the Emperor climbed Du'an Mountain, lingered over the relics of the first Qishi Khan, and paced there looking back, moved to deep sighs.

sentences.zh: 聞獄官涅離擅造大校，人不堪其苦，有至死者，命誅之。

translations.literal: Hearing the prison officer Nieli had arbitrarily devised a great cangue, people could not bear the suffering and some died from it; he ordered him executed.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that the jailer Nieli had on his own authority fashioned a massive cangue, torment so fierce that men died under it, he ordered Nieli put to death.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，次狼河，獲逆黨雅裏、弭裏，生埋之銅河南軌下。

translations.literal: On day renchen, he halted at Lang River; captured rebels Yali and Mili were buried alive beneath the rails south of the Tong River.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen day he encamped at Lang River; the captured rebels Yali and Mili were buried alive under the track south of the Tong River.

sentences.zh: 放所俘還，多為於骨裏所掠。

translations.literal: Released captives were sent back; many were seized by the Yuguri.
translations.idiomatic: Freed prisoners were sent on their way, but many were snatched up again by the Yuguri.

sentences.zh: 上怒，引輕騎馳擊。

translations.literal: The Emperor in anger led light cavalry in swift attack.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, the Emperor himself galloped out with light horse to strike them.

sentences.zh: 復遣驍將分道追襲，盡獲其眾並掠者。

translations.literal: He again sent crack generals on separate routes to pursue and raid, capturing all their force together with the plunderers.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent fierce commanders by separate paths to hunt them down, taking every man of theirs along with the looters.

sentences.zh: 庚子，次阿敦濼，以養子涅裏思附諸弟叛，以鬼箭射殺之。

translations.literal: On day gengzi, he halted at Adun Marsh; because his adopted son Nielisi had joined the younger brothers in rebellion, he was shot to death with ghost-arrows.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi day he stopped at Adun Marsh; his adopted son Nielisi, who had sided with the rebel brothers, was executed by ghost-arrow.

sentences.zh: 其餘黨六千，各以輕重論刑。

translations.literal: The remaining six thousand partisans were each sentenced according to the severity of their crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Six thousand remaining accomplices were punished each according to the weight of his offense.

sentences.zh: 於厥掠生口者三十餘人，亦俾贖其罪，放歸本部。

translations.literal: More than thirty of the Yuqi who had seized captives were also allowed to ransom their guilt and were released to their districts.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty-odd Yuqi who had carried off prisoners were likewise permitted to buy back their guilt and return to their tribes.

sentences.zh: 至石嶺西，詔收回軍乏食所棄兵仗，召北府兵驗而還之。

translations.literal: Reaching west of Shiling, he ordered recovered the weapons abandoned when the returning army lacked food, summoned Northern Prefecture soldiers to verify and return them.
translations.idiomatic: West of Shiling he commanded that arms cast aside for want of food on the march home be gathered in; Northern Prefecture troops were called to identify and reclaim them.

sentences.zh: 以夷離涅裏袞附諸弟為叛，不忍顯戮，命自投崖而死。

translations.literal: Because Yilie Nielihun had joined the younger brothers in rebellion, unable to bear public execution, he was ordered to throw himself from a cliff and die.
translations.idiomatic: Yilie Nielihun, who had followed the brothers into revolt, the Emperor could not bear to kill before the court; he was commanded to cast himself from a cliff.

sentences.zh: 秋八月己卯，幸龍眉宮，逆黨二十九人，以其妻女賜有功將校，所掠珍寶、孳畜還主；

translations.literal: In the eighth month of autumn, on day jimao, he visited Longmei Palace; twenty-nine rebels—their wives and daughters were bestowed on meritorious officers and commanders; stolen treasures and livestock were returned to owners;
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth autumn month, on jimao day, he went to Longmei Palace. Twenty-nine rebels' wives and daughters were given to deserving officers; plundered gems and herds were restored to their owners;

sentences.zh: 亡其本物者，命責償其家；

translations.literal: those who had lost their original goods were ordered to make restitution to their households;
translations.idiomatic: where the original property was gone, the culprits were ordered to compensate the households;

sentences.zh: 不能償者，賜以其部曲。

translations.literal: those who could not pay were granted the rebel's followers in compensation.
translations.idiomatic: those who could not pay were awarded the rebels' retainers in lieu.

sentences.zh: 九月壬戌，上發自西樓。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on day renxu, the Emperor departed from Xilou.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on renxu day, the Emperor set out from Xilou.

sentences.zh: 冬十月庚午。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter, on day gengwu.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, in the tenth month, on gengwu day.

sentences.zh: 駐赤崖。

translations.literal: He encamped at Chiya.
translations.idiomatic: He made camp at Chiya.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，和州回鶻來貢。

translations.literal: On day wuyin, the Huihu of Hezhou came to pay tribute.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin day the Uighurs of Hezhou arrived with tribute.

sentences.zh: 癸未，乙室府人迪裏古、迷骨離部人特裏以從逆誅。

translations.literal: On day guimwei, Diligu of Yishi Prefecture and Teli of the Migulii tribe were executed for joining the rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: On guimwei day Diligu of Yishi Prefecture and Teli of the Migulii tribe were put to death for following the revolt.

sentences.zh: 詔群臣分決滯訟，以韓知古錄其事，只裏姑掌捕亡。

translations.literal: He decreed that ministers divide and decide backlogged lawsuits; Han Zhigu was to record the proceedings; Zhiliggu was to manage the pursuit of fugitives.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the ministers to divide and clear stalled cases; Han Zhigu was to keep the record, and Zhiliggu to hunt down fugitives.

sentences.zh: 十一月，祠木葉山。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, he sacrificed at Mount Muye.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month he offered sacrifice at Mount Muye.

sentences.zh: 還次昭烏山，省風俗，見高年，議朝政，定吉凶儀。

translations.literal: Returning he halted at Zhaowu Mountain, inspected local customs, received the aged, discussed court policy, and fixed auspicious and inauspicious rites.
translations.idiomatic: On the return he stopped at Zhaowu Mountain, reviewed local ways, received the elderly, debated state affairs, and settled the rites of fortune and misfortune.

sentences.zh: 十二月戊子，燔柴於蓮花濼。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on day wuzi, he burned sacrificial wood at Lotus Marsh.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on wuzi day, he burned sacrificial wood at Lotus Marsh.

sentences.zh: 八年春正月甲辰，以曷魯為迭剌部夷離，忽烈為惕隱。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, on day jiachen in the first month of spring, Helu was made Yilie of the Yelie Tribe, and Hulie was made Tiyin.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, on jiachen day of the first spring month, Helu was appointed yilie of the Yelie tribe and Hulie was made tiyin.

sentences.zh: 於骨裏部人特離敏執逆党怖胡、亞裏只等十七人來獻，上親鞫之。

translations.literal: Telimin of the Yuguri tribe seized rebel partisans Buhu, Yalizhi, and seventeen others and presented them; the Emperor personally interrogated them.
translations.idiomatic: Telimin of the Yuguri tribe captured seventeen rebels including Buhu and Yalizhi and brought them in; the Emperor examined them himself.

sentences.zh: 辭多連宗室及有脅從者，乃杖殺首惡怖胡，餘並原釋。

translations.literal: Their confessions implicated many in the imperial clan and those who had been coerced; therefore the chief villain Buhu was beaten to death, and the rest were all pardoned and released.
translations.idiomatic: Their testimony dragged in many clansmen and men who had been forced along; the ringleader Buhu was beaten to death, and all the rest were forgiven and freed.

sentences.zh: 於越率懶之子化哥屢蓄奸謀，上每優容之，而反覆不悛，召父老群臣正其罪，並其子戮之，分其財以給衛士。

translations.literal: Yuyue Shuilian's son Huage repeatedly harbored treacherous designs; the Emperor always treated him with forbearance, yet he turned back again and would not repent; summoning elder leaders and ministers to fix his guilt, both he and his son were executed, and their property was divided to supply the guards.
translations.idiomatic: Huage, son of Yuyue Shuilian, nursed treason again and again; the Emperor repeatedly indulged him, yet he relapsed and would not mend. Elders and ministers were summoned to judge his crime; he and his son were both slain, and their goods were split among the guards.

sentences.zh: 有司所鞫逆黨三百餘人，獄既具，上以人命至重，死不復生，賜宴一日，隨其平生之好，使為之。

translations.literal: The officials had interrogated more than three hundred rebels; when the case was complete, the Emperor, considering human life supremely weighty and that the dead cannot live again, granted them a banquet for one day, allowing each according to his lifelong preferences.
translations.idiomatic: The courts had tried more than three hundred rebels; when the dossiers were complete, the Emperor, holding life most precious and knowing the dead do not return, gave them one last feast, each man indulged in what he had loved in life.

sentences.zh: 酒酣，或歌、或舞、或戲射、角，各極其意。

translations.literal: When the wine had deepened, some sang, some danced, some sported at archery or wrestling—each to the full of his desire.
translations.idiomatic: As the cups went round, some sang, some danced, some shot for sport or wrestled—each to the limit of his wish.

sentences.zh: 明日，乃以輕重論刑。

translations.literal: The next day, sentences were passed according to severity.
translations.idiomatic: The next day punishments were meted out by degree.

sentences.zh: 首惡剌葛，其次迭剌哥，上猶弟之，不忍置法，杖而釋之。

translations.literal: Chief villain Cige, next Dieci Ge—the Emperor still regarded them as brothers, unwilling to apply the law; he beat them and released them.
translations.idiomatic: Cige was chief among the guilty, Dieci Ge next; the Emperor still called them brothers and could not bear the full penalty—he flogged them and let them go.

sentences.zh: 以寅底石、安端性本庸弱，為剌葛所使，皆釋其罪。

translations.literal: Because Yindishi and Anduan were by nature mediocre and weak, used by Cige, all their guilt was released.
translations.idiomatic: Yindishi and Anduan, being dull and easily led, had acted at Cige's bidding; their crimes were all remitted.

sentences.zh: 前于越赫底裏子解裏、剌葛妻轄剌已實預逆謀，命皆絞殺之。

translations.literal: The former Yuyue Hedili's son Jieli and Cige's wife Xiala Yi had truly participated in the plot; both were ordered strangled.
translations.idiomatic: Jieli, son of the former yuyue Hedili, and Cige's wife Xiala Yi had truly shared in the plot; both were ordered strangled.

sentences.zh: 寅底石妻涅離脅從，安端妻粘睦姑嘗有忠告，並免。

translations.literal: Yindishi's wife Nieli had been coerced; Anduan's wife Nianmugu had once offered loyal advice—all were exempted.
translations.idiomatic: Yindishi's wife Nieli had been forced along; Anduan's wife Nianmugu had once warned in good faith—both were spared.

sentences.zh: 因謂左右曰：「諸弟性雖敏黠，而蓄奸稔惡。

translations.literal: He then said to those nearby: "My younger brothers, though by nature clever and sharp, long stored treachery and accumulated wickedness.
translations.idiomatic: He then told those at his side: "My brothers are quick and clever, yet they hoarded treachery and piled up evil.

sentences.zh: 嘗自矜有出人之智，安忍凶狠，溪壑可塞而貪黷無厭。

translations.literal: They once prided themselves on wisdom surpassing others; cruel and fierce without qualm; gorges and ravines may be filled, yet greed and corruption know no satiety.
translations.idiomatic: They boasted of wisdom above other men, ruthless and savage without restraint; though gorges may be filled, their greed never knew its fill.

sentences.zh: 求人之失，雖小而可恕，謂重如泰山；

translations.literal: Seeking others' faults—even small ones that could be forgiven—they called as weighty as Mount Tai;
translations.idiomatic: Hunting others' faults, they treated the smallest slip, easily pardoned, as heavy as Mount Tai;

sentences.zh: 身行不義，雖入大惡，謂輕於鴻毛。

translations.literal: their own unrighteous conduct, even entering into great evil, they deemed lighter than a goose feather.
translations.idiomatic: their own wrongdoing, even when it sank into deepest crime, they called lighter than a goose down.

sentences.zh: 昵比群小，謀及婦人，同惡相濟，以危國祚。

translations.literal: Clinging to petty men, plotting with women, aiding one another in evil, thereby endangering the fate of the state.
translations.idiomatic: They kept company with low men, schemed with women, and helped one another in wickedness until the throne itself was threatened.

sentences.zh: 雖欲不敗，其可得乎？

translations.literal: Even if one wished them not to fail—how could it be attained?
translations.idiomatic: If one wished them not to ruin themselves—how could such a wish be granted?

sentences.zh: 北宰相實魯妻餘盧睹姑於國至親，一旦負朕，從於叛逆，未置之法而病死。

translations.literal: Northern Chancellor Shilu's wife Yuludugu was among the nation's closest kin; in a single day she betrayed me and joined the rebellion; before law could be applied she died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Chancellor Shilu's wife Yuludugu stood among my nearest kin; in a day she turned against me and joined the rebels; before sentence could fall, sickness took her.

sentences.zh: 此天誅也。

translations.literal: This was Heaven's punishment.
translations.idiomatic: That was Heaven's judgment.

sentences.zh: 解裏自幼與朕常同寢食，眷遇之厚，冠於宗屬，亦與其父背大恩而從不軌，茲可恕乎！」

translations.literal: Jieli from youth constantly shared bed and board with me; the favor shown him topped all the clan; yet together with his father he turned against great kindness to follow wrong paths—can this be forgiven!"
translations.idiomatic: Jieli from boyhood ate and slept at my side; no kinsman knew a kindness like his—yet he and his father repaid deep grace with rebellion. How could that be forgiven!"

sentences.zh: 秋七月丙申朔，有司上諸帳族與謀逆者三百餘人罪狀，皆棄市。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of autumn, on the bingshen new moon, officials submitted the charges of more than three hundred clansmen who plotted rebellion; all were executed in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh autumn month, on the bingshen new moon, the courts reported the crimes of more than three hundred tent-kin who had joined the plot; all were put to death in the market.

sentences.zh: 上歎曰：「致人於死，豈朕所欲。

translations.literal: The Emperor sighed: "Bringing men to death—how is that what I desire?
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor sighed: "To send men to their deaths—is that my wish?

sentences.zh: 若止負朕躬，尚可容貸。

translations.literal: Had they only wronged my person, pardon might still be granted.
translations.idiomatic: Had they merely wronged me alone, mercy might still have been possible.

sentences.zh: 此曹恣行不道，殘害忠良，塗炭生民，剽掠財產。

translations.literal: This lot wantonly pursued the wayless path, slaughtered the loyal and good, scorched the living people, plundered property.
translations.idiomatic: But this crowd ran riot in lawlessness, butchered the loyal, burned the people alive, and stripped their goods.

sentences.zh: 民間昔有萬馬，今皆徒步，有國以來所未嘗有。

translations.literal: Among the people, where once there were ten thousand horses, all now went on foot—unprecedented since the founding of the state.
translations.idiomatic: Where the commons once kept ten thousand horses between them, now all went on foot—a thing never seen since the realm was founded.

sentences.zh: 實不得已而誅之。」

translations.literal: Truly there was no choice but to put them to death."
translations.idiomatic: I had no choice but to kill them."

sentences.zh: 冬十月甲子朔，建開皇殿於明王樓基。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter, on the jiazi new moon, the Kaihuang Hall was built on the foundation of the Bright King Tower.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, in the tenth month, on the jiazi new moon, Kaihuang Hall was raised on the old site of the Bright King Tower.

sentences.zh: 九年春正月，烏古部叛，討平之。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, in the first month of spring, the Wugu tribe rebelled; he campaigned and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, in the first spring month, the Wugu tribe rose; he marched against them and brought them to heel.

sentences.zh: 夏六月，幽州軍校齊行本舉其族及其部曲男女三千人請降，詔授檢校尚書、左僕射，賜名兀欲，給其堿食。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of summer, Youzhou military officer Qi Xingben led his clan and his followers—men and women, three thousand in all—to request surrender; by decree he was appointed Acting Minister of the Secretariat, Left Vice Director, granted the name Wuyu, and supplied with rations.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth summer month, Qi Xingben, an officer of Youzhou, came over with his clan and retainers, three thousand souls in all; by edict he was named Acting Minister of the Secretariat and Left Vice Director, given the name Wuyu, and granted provisions for his people.

sentences.zh: 數日亡去，幽帥周德威納之。

translations.literal: After several days he fled away; Youzhou commander Zhou Dewei received him.
translations.idiomatic: Within days he slipped away, and Zhou Dewei, commander of Youzhou, took him in.

sentences.zh: 及詔索之，德威語不遜，乃議南征。

translations.literal: When an edict came demanding his return, Dewei spoke insolently, and a southern campaign was then debated.
translations.idiomatic: When the court ordered him handed back, Dewei answered with insolence, and the court began to plan a campaign south.

sentences.zh: 冬十月戊申，鉤魚于鴨淥江。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter, on day wushen, he went ice fishing on the Yalu River.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, in the tenth month, on wushen day, he went ice fishing on the Yalu River.

sentences.zh: 新羅遣使貢方物，高麗遣使進寶劍，吳越王錢遣滕彥休來貢。

translations.literal: Silla sent envoys bearing tribute goods; Goryeo sent envoys presenting a precious sword; the King of Wuyue, Qian, sent Teng Yanxiu with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Silla sent envoys with regional products; Goryeo sent envoys bearing a treasured sword; and Qian, King of Wuyue, dispatched Teng Yanxiu with tribute.

sentences.zh: 是歲，君基太一神數見，詔圖其像。

translations.literal: That year the Junji Taiyi deity appeared repeatedly; an edict ordered his likeness painted.
translations.idiomatic: That year the Junji Taiyi god was seen again and again, and the Emperor ordered his image drawn.

sentences.zh: 三月丙辰，以迭烈部夷離曷魯為阿廬朵裏於越，百僚進秩、頒賚有差，賜三日。

translations.literal: On day bingchen in the third month, Helu, yilijin of the Dieci branch, was made Aluduo li yuyue; the hundred officials were advanced in rank and rewards distributed in varying measure, and a three-day grant was bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen day in the third month, Helu, yilijin of the Dieci branch, was appointed Aluduo li yuyue; officials were promoted and gifts handed out in due measure, and the court granted three days' leave.

sentences.zh: 立子倍為皇太子。

translations.literal: His son Bei was installed as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: His son Bei was named crown prince.

sentences.zh: 夏四月乙酉朔，晉幽州節度使盧國用來降，<八>以為幽州兵馬留後。

translations.literal: On the yiyou new moon in the fourth month of summer, Lu Guoyong, Jin's military governor of Youzhou, came to surrender; <8> he was made Youzhou military and cavalry acting commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On the yiyou new moon of the fourth summer month, Lu Guoyong, Jin's governor of Youzhou, defected; <8> he was appointed acting military and cavalry commissioner of Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，梁遣郎公遠來賀。

translations.literal: On day jiachen, Liang sent Lang Gongyuan to offer congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen day Liang dispatched Lang Gongyuan with congratulations.

sentences.zh: 六月庚寅，吳越王遣滕彥休來貢。

translations.literal: On day gengyin in the sixth month, the King of Wuyue sent Teng Yanxiu with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin day in the sixth month, the King of Wuyue sent Teng Yanxiu with tribute.

sentences.zh: 秋七月壬申，親征突厥、吐渾、項、小蕃、沙陀諸部，皆平之。

translations.literal: On day renshen in the seventh month of autumn, he personally campaigned against the Turks, Tuguhun, Xiang, Lesser Fan, Shatuo, and other tribes, and pacified them all.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen day in the seventh autumn month he took the field in person against the Turks, Tuguhun, Xiang, Lesser Fan, Shatuo, and the rest, and brought them all to heel.

sentences.zh: 俘其酋長及其戶萬五千六百，鎧甲、兵仗、器服九十餘萬，寶貨、駝馬、牛羊不可勝算。

translations.literal: He captured their chieftains together with fifteen thousand six hundred households, more than nine hundred thousand suits of armor, weapons, and gear, and treasure, camels, horses, cattle, and sheep beyond reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: He took their chieftains and fifteen thousand six hundred households captive, along with more than nine hundred thousand pieces of armor, arms, and equipment, and treasure, camels, horses, cattle, and sheep past all count.

sentences.zh: 八月，撥朔州，擒節度使李嗣本。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, he seized Shuozhou and captured its military governor Li Siben.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he overran Shuozhou and took its governor Li Siben prisoner.

sentences.zh: 勒石紀功於青塚南。

translations.literal: He carved stone to record the achievement south of the Green Mound.
translations.idiomatic: He had his victory cut in stone south of the Green Mound.

sentences.zh: 冬十月癸未朔，乘勝而東。

translations.literal: On the guiwei new moon in the tenth month of winter, riding the victory he marched east.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, on the guiwei new moon of the tenth month, he pressed east while the momentum held.

sentences.zh: 十一月，攻蔚、新、武、媯、儒五州，斬首萬四千七百餘級。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, he attacked the five prefectures of Yu, Xin, Wu, Gui, and Ru, and took more than fourteen thousand seven hundred heads.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month he struck Yu, Xin, Wu, Gui, and Ru—five prefectures in all—and claimed more than fourteen thousand seven hundred heads.

sentences.zh: 自代北至河曲陰山，盡有其地。

translations.literal: From north of Dai to the Yin Mountains at the river bend, he held all the land.
translations.idiomatic: From north of Dai to the Yin Mountains along the river bend, the whole country fell to him.

sentences.zh: 遂改武州為歸化州，媯州為可汗州，置西南面招討司，選有功者領之。

translations.literal: He then changed Wu Prefecture to Guihua Prefecture and Gui Prefecture to Khan Prefecture, established the Southwest Pacification Office, and chose men of merit to command it.
translations.idiomatic: He renamed Wu Prefecture Guihua Prefecture and Gui Prefecture Khan Prefecture, set up a Southwest Pacification Office, and put proven men in charge.

sentences.zh: 其圍蔚州，敵樓無故自壞，眾軍大噪乘之，不時而破。

translations.literal: When they invested Yu Prefecture, the enemy towers collapsed for no reason; the army raised a great clamor and pressed the chance, and the city fell before long.
translations.idiomatic: At the siege of Yu Prefecture the watchtowers gave way without cause; the troops broke into a roar and rushed the breach, and the city fell in no time.

sentences.zh: 時梁及吳越二使皆在焉，詔引環城觀之，因賜滕彥休名曰逑呂。

translations.literal: At that time envoys from both Liang and Wuyue were present; by edict they were led around the city to watch, and Teng Yanxiu was granted the name Qiulü.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys from Liang and Wuyue were there at the time; the Emperor had them led around the walls to witness the fall, and bestowed on Teng Yanxiu the name Qiulü.

sentences.zh: 十二月，收山北八軍。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, he recovered the eight armies north of the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he retook the eight armies north of the mountains.

sentences.zh: 二年春二月，晉新州裨將盧文進殺節度使李存榘來降。

translations.literal: In the second month of spring in the second year, Lu Wenjin, Jin's deputy general of Xin Prefecture, killed military governor Li Cunju and came to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, in the second spring month, Lu Wenjin, a Jin deputy commander at Xin Prefecture, killed Governor Li Cunju and defected.

sentences.zh: 進攻其城，刺史安金全遁，以文進部將劉殷為刺史。

translations.literal: Advancing to attack the city, Prefect An Jinquan fled; Wenjin's subordinate general Liu Yin was made prefect.
translations.idiomatic: He marched on the city; Prefect An Jinquan fled, and Wenjin's officer Liu Yin was installed as prefect.

sentences.zh: 三月辛亥，攻幽州，節度使周德威以幽、并、鎮、定、魏五州之兵拒於居庸關之西，合戰於新州東，大破之，斬首三萬餘級，殺李嗣恩之子武八。

translations.literal: On day xinhai in the third month, he attacked Youzhou; military governor Zhou Dewei, with troops from the five prefectures of You, Bing, Zhen, Ding, and Wei, blocked him west of Juyong Pass; they joined battle east of Xin Prefecture, routed him utterly, took more than thirty thousand heads, and killed Li Si'en's son Wuba.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai day in the third month he invested Youzhou. Zhou Dewei, governor of Youzhou, barred the way west of Juyong Pass with forces from You, Bing, Zhen, Ding, and Wei; east of Xin Prefecture they met in battle, broke the Khitan host, took more than thirty thousand heads, and killed Wuba, son of Li Si'en.

sentences.zh: <九>以后弟阿骨只為統軍，實魯為先鋒，東出關略燕、趙，不遇敵而還。

translations.literal: <9> Thereafter his younger brother Aguqi was made commander-in-chief and Shilu vanguard; they marched east out of the pass to sweep Yan and Zhao, met no enemy, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: <9> Then his brother Aguqi was made supreme commander and Shilu led the van; they went east through the pass to overrun Yan and Zhao, found no foe, and turned back.

sentences.zh: 己未，於骨裏叛，命室魯以兵討之。

translations.literal: On day jiwei, Yuguli rebelled; Shilu was ordered to take troops and punish him.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei day Yuguli rose in revolt, and Shilu was sent with troops to suppress him.

sentences.zh: 夏四月壬午，圍幽州，不克。

translations.literal: On day renwu in the fourth month of summer, he invested Youzhou but could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu day in the fourth summer month he besieged Youzhou and failed to capture it.

sentences.zh: 六月乙巳，望城中有氣如煙火狀，上曰：「未可攻也。

translations.literal: On day yisi in the sixth month, gazing at the city he saw vapor like smoke and fire; the Emperor said: "It is not yet time to attack.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi day in the sixth month he looked at the city and saw a vapor like smoke and flame; the Emperor said, "We must not attack yet.

sentences.zh: 」以大暑霖潦，班師。

translations.literal: " Because of great heat and torrential rains, the army withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: " With the midsummer heat and ceaseless rain, he drew the army off.

sentences.zh: 留曷魯、盧國用守之。

translations.literal: Helu and Lu Guoyong were left to hold it.
translations.idiomatic: Helu and Lu Guoyong were left to garrison the place.

sentences.zh: 剌葛與其子賽保裏叛入幽州。

translations.literal: Lige and his son Saibaoli rebelled and entered Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Lige and his son Saibaoli defected and fled into Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 秋八月，李存遣李嗣源等救幽州，曷魯等以兵少而還。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of autumn, Li Cun sent Li Siyuan and others to relieve Youzhou; Helu and the rest withdrew for lack of numbers.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth autumn month Li Cun dispatched Li Siyuan and others to rescue Youzhou, and Helu and his fellows pulled back for want of men.

sentences.zh: 三年春正月丙申，以皇弟安端為大內惕隱，命攻雲州及西南諸部。

translations.literal: On day bingshen in the first month of spring in the third year, his imperial brother Anduan was made Great Inner tiyin and ordered to attack Yun Prefecture and the southwestern tribes.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, on bingshen day of the first spring month, his brother Anduan was appointed Great Inner tiyin and charged to attack Yun Prefecture and the tribes of the southwest.

sentences.zh: 二月，達旦國來聘。

translations.literal: In the second month, the Dadan state sent envoys on a friendly visit.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month the Dadan kingdom sent envoys on a courtesy mission.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，城皇都，以禮部尚書康默記充版築使。

translations.literal: On day guihai, the imperial capital was walled; Minister of Rites Kang Mojie was made commissioner of construction.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai day they walled the imperial capital, and Kang Mojie, Minister of Rites, was put in charge of the work.

sentences.zh: 梁遣使來聘。

translations.literal: Liang sent envoys on a friendly visit.
translations.idiomatic: Liang sent envoys on a courtesy mission.

sentences.zh: 晉、吳越、渤海、高麗、回鶻、阻卜、項及幽、鎮、定、魏、潞等州各遣使來貢。

translations.literal: Jin, Wuyue, Bohai, Goryeo, Uighur, Zubu, Xiang, and the prefectures of You, Zhen, Ding, Wei, Lu, and others each sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Jin, Wuyue, Bohai, Goryeo, the Uighurs, the Zubu, the Xiang, and the prefectures of You, Zhen, Ding, Wei, Lu, and the rest all sent tribute envoys.

sentences.zh: 夏四月乙巳，皇弟迭烈哥謀叛，事覺，知有罪當誅，預為營壙，而諸戚請免。

translations.literal: On day yisi in the fourth month of summer, his imperial brother Dielege plotted rebellion; the affair was discovered; knowing guilt deserved death, he prepared a grave pit in advance, yet the kinsmen pleaded for pardon.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi day in the fourth summer month his brother Dielege conspired to rebel; the plot came to light. Knowing he deserved death, he had a burial pit dug beforehand, but his clansmen begged for mercy.

sentences.zh: 上素惡其弟寅底石妻涅裏袞，乃曰：「涅裏袞能代其死，則從。

translations.literal: The Emperor had long hated the wife of his brother Yindishi, Nieligun, and therefore said: "If Nieligun can die in his stead, then I will consent.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor had always loathed his brother Yindishi's wife Nieligun, and said, "If Nieligun will die in his place, I will agree.

sentences.zh: 」涅裏袞自縊壙中，並以奴女古、叛人曷魯只生瘞其中。

translations.literal: " Nieligun hanged herself in the pit, and the slave Nügu and the rebel Heluzhi were buried alive there with her.
translations.idiomatic: " Nieligun strangled herself in the pit, and the bondservant Nügu and the traitor Heluzhi were entombed alive beside her.

sentences.zh: 遂赦迭烈哥。

translations.literal: Dielege was then pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Dielege was then forgiven.

sentences.zh: 五月乙亥，詔建孔子廟、佛寺、道觀。

translations.literal: On day yihai in the fifth month, an edict ordered temples built to Confucius, to the Buddha, and to the Dao.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai day in the fifth month he decreed the building of a Confucian temple, Buddhist monasteries, and Daoist abbeys.

translations.literal: Collation Notes
translations.idiomatic: Collation Notes

sentences.zh: 一：霞瀨益石烈張元濟校勘記

translations.literal: 1: Xi Laiyi Shilie — Zhang Yuanji's collation notes
translations.idiomatic: 1: Xi Laiyi Shilie — Zhang Yuanji's collation notes

sentences.zh: （以下稱張校）〉

translations.literal: (hereinafter abbreviated as Zhang Collation)]〉
translations.idiomatic: (hereinafter abbreviated as Zhang Collation)]〉

sentences.zh: 引百官志一「石烈，縣也」，百官志二「弭裏，鄉也」，謂石烈下不應綴鄉字。

translations.literal: Citing Officials' Register, vol. 1, "shilie means county," and Officials' Register, vol. 2, "milai means township," he argues that the character for township should not follow after shilie.
translations.idiomatic: He cites Officials' Register, vol. 1 — "shilie is a county" — and vol. 2 — "milai is a township" — and holds that the township character should not be appended after shilie.

sentences.zh: 按國語解又以石烈為鄉，弭裏為鄉之小者。

translations.literal: According to the Explanation of the National Language, shilie is also a township, and milai is a smaller subdivision of township.
translations.idiomatic: The Explanation of the National Language, however, also defines shilie as a township and milai as a smaller township unit.

sentences.zh: 石烈鄉，鄉字亦復贅。

translations.literal: In "shilie township," the character for township is likewise redundant.
translations.idiomatic: In "shilie township," the word township is redundant as well.

sentences.zh: 檢下文太祖七年六月轄賴縣、營衛志下六院部轄懶石烈，均此名異譯。

translations.literal: Checking the text below, Taizu year seven, sixth month, Xialai County, and in Guards Record, lower section, Six Yuan Department, Xialan Shilie — all are variant renderings of this same name.
translations.idiomatic: Below, in Taizu's seventh year, sixth month, Xialai County, and in the lower section of the Guards Record, Six Yuan Department, Xialan Shilie — each is a variant translation of the same name.

sentences.zh: 鄉字衍。

translations.literal: The character for township is spurious.
translations.idiomatic: The township character is a spurious addition.

sentences.zh: 二：伐河東代北代北，原誤「伐北」，據兵衛志上及永樂大典

translations.literal: 2: "Campaign against Hedong and northern Dai" — northern Dai; the original text erroneously read "northern campaign," corrected according to Military Guards Record, upper section, and the Yongle Encyclopedia
translations.idiomatic: 2: "Campaign against Hedong and northern Dai" — for northern Dai, the original erroneously read "northern campaign"; the correction follows Military Guards Record, upper section, and the Yongle Encyclopedia

sentences.zh: （道光殿本考證引）〉

translations.idiomatic: (cited in the textual verification of the Daoguang Hall edition)]〉

sentences.zh: 改。

translations.literal: Corrected accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Corrected accordingly.

sentences.zh: 三：如迂王集會堝紀太宗天顯五年十月作如迂正集會堝。

translations.literal: 3: Ru'erwang Assembly Mound — the Record of Taizong's fifth year, tenth month, reads Ru'erzheng Assembly Mound.
translations.idiomatic: 3: Ru'erwang Assembly Mound — the account of Taizong's tenth month in the fifth year reads Ru'erzheng Assembly Mound.

sentences.zh: 四：夏四月丁未朔唐梁王朱全忠廢其主尋弑之錢大昕廿二史考異

translations.literal: 4: On the dingwei new moon in the fourth month of summer, Tang's Liang King Zhu Quanzhong deposed his sovereign and soon murdered him — Qian Daxin's Examination of Discrepancies in the Twenty-Two Histories
translations.idiomatic: 4: On the dingwei new moon of the fourth summer month, Zhu Quanzhong, Liang King of Tang, deposed his lord and soon killed him — Qian Daxin's Examination of Discrepancies in the Twenty-Two Histories

sentences.zh: （以下稱考異）〉

translations.idiomatic: (hereinafter abbreviated as Examination of Discrepancies)]〉

translations.literal: Citing Ouyang Xiu's Historical Records of the Five Dynasties
translations.idiomatic: Citing Ouyang Xiu's Historical Records of the Five Dynasties
